whyWatch.body:
This is the first 48-team World Cup in history, with 104 matches across 3 countries. Tubi has 2 live matches, both group openers, both free. There's also a documentary already following players on the road to the tournament, plus Fox Sports FIFA content, highlights, and replays to fill in everything around it.

If you're planning to watch the live matches in real time, make the free account before June 11. If replays, highlights, or Destination World Cup 2026 are more your speed, you can start watching right now without signing in.

items.heading: Live matches, June 11 and June 12
items.paragraph: Mexico vs. South Africa kicks off at 1:00 PM CT on June 11 at Mexico City Stadium. USA vs. Paraguay follows at 6:00 PM PT on June 12 at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood. Both are group stage openers, and both stream free with a Tubi account. Fox Pregame runs before each match, with post-game coverage following the June 12 final whistle.

items.heading: VOD replays and highlights
items.paragraph: Miss a live match? The full 90-minute replay goes up within 1 to 2 hours after the final whistle and doesn't require sign-in. The hub also has 4-minute highlights, vertical video versions for mobile, and 30-minute extended highlights when you want a fuller catch-up without sitting through the whole thing.

items.heading: Destination World Cup 2026, streaming now
items.paragraph: This Tubi-exclusive documentary follows Marc Cucurella, Harry Wilson, and Weston McKennie as they chase a place in the 2026 World Cup. Episode 1 is 23 minutes and already live. McKennie appears in the documentary and then suits up for the USMNT on June 12, which makes the series a natural way to get into the match before it happens.

items.heading: Fox Sports FIFA library
items.paragraph: Beyond the 2 live matches, the hub includes Fox Sports FIFA VOD content, clips, and linear programming. If you want more context heading into the openers, or just more to watch between matches, it's all in one place.
